assumed_parameters.source: docs/HARDWARE-MODELS.md local DRAM preset, capacity overridden for this test

limitations: Fabric: links, pools, and switches are FIFO byte servers; transfers occupy every hop on their static route plus the destination tier.
Replay: ops execute in (ts_ns, file order); same-timestamp ops batch by (kind, bytes).
Observed placement (migrate/prefetch/evict rows, tier hints) is never replayed as directives; the configured policy recomputes all placement.
Capacity overcommit halts replay with the first offending row (no silent divergence).
Prefetch (when enabled) follows trailing-integer stride, shares demand fabric, and reports accuracy = touched-after-issue / issued (strictly later timestamps).
Multi-page reservations place atomically (all local or all on one remote tier).
Clean evictions transfer 0 bytes; only dirty pages write back.

Ops with an explicit node run there; ops without one follow their request's round-robin shard. Placement is single-owner N-tier: non-owners read through without moving the page; there is no replication and no coherence protocol.
scenario_assumptions: Local capacity is intentionally set to 2 GiB to force overflow. A real H100 node has far more DRAM; this scenario exists only to exercise the remote path.
One compute node and one shared pool keep the event stream small enough to inspect by hand.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode derived from Llama-3-70B geometry, not a captured trace.
The compute tokens_per_second field is omitted, matching examples/llama-70b-cxl.json. Request duration is therefore driven by modeled memory accesses, not accelerator throughput.
